transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-07 15:30 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Nina (Redwood CSM), Dr. Maya Chen (CTO, Aperture), Liam O'Neill (Head of Platform), Priya Kapoor (Security)

Auto Summary: quick renewal cadence check, region onboarding plan, security gating items, agree next steps.

00:00 Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you squeezing this in. How's the afternoon on your side, Maya?
00:05 Maya (CTO): Yeah, pretty good. We wanted to run through the renewal terms and the EU staging plan — and make sure KMS and SOC2 stuff is in place before we sign the amendment.
00:14 Jordan: Great, that's exactly what we planned to cover. Quick readout: Nina and I put together an updated commitment sketch and options for burst. Samir has notes on latency/benchmarks for the eu-west queue.
00:25 Samir (SE): Hi all — quick intro; I'll be leading the short performance plan. We tested some internal patterns and have an approach to simulate your 1k–3k token inference patterns.
00:33 Liam (Head of Platform): Perfect. Our main gating questions are: 1) can you guarantee median P95 under 550ms for chat flows at our committed qps? 2) can we run this in our VPC (private) rather than public hosted endpoints?
00:46 Samir: Good q. For P95 — with Dedicated pools we hit sub-400ms fairly consistently on comparable models in our benchmarks, but that depends on batch size, kv cache hit rate, and quantization. For hosted variants, P95 is generally higher, but we have routing and fallback policies.
00:58 Priya (Security): When you say Dedicated, are we talking Redwood Dedicated in a Redwood-managed subnet, or a private deployment inside our VPC? We need clarity because KMS keys and HSM-bound attestations are only acceptable in VPC/on-prem.
01:10 Jordan: Right — we split this two ways: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPUs) gives isolation at the tenant level but still runs in Redwood network; Redwood Private is the VPC/on-prem with customer-managed networking and KMS. For contract amendment we can add dedicated capacity now and plan Private onboarding later.
01:22 Maya: Timeline is important. We want committed capacity for Q1 and EU staging by end of January. Is that realistic?
01:30 Nina (CSM): January end is tight but plausible if we lock the commitment this month. Provisioning for dedicated capacity usually takes 2–3 weeks once PO is in. Private/VPC onboarding has more steps — network tests, KMS, and a security review — usually 4–6 weeks.
01:44 Liam: Okay so commit now for dedicated for throughput, while we run security gating for VPC — that seems fine.
01:49 Jordan: Exactly — typical path is commit to Dedicated for performance and guaranteed qps, then a staged Private pilot for data sovereignty. We'll include a migration clause in the SOW so you're not double-billed.
01:59 Maya: About pricing: last year's rates don't look favorable with our current usage pattern. We need a model that includes committed tokens + burst. Can you show the math?
02:10 Jordan: We'll send a revised pricing sheet. High-level: committed unit price has a discount; burst is billed at a higher rate but with a cap. Nina put together two options: a 12-month commit with burst headroom vs a 6-month entry with tighter caps.
02:24 Nina: I'll include an explicit example with your average qps and token distribution to show net monthly spend in each option.
02:31 Priya: Security docs — SOC2 attestation, pen test summary, audit logs retention — we need those to route through legal. Also KMS integration docs showing envelope encryption and key lifecycle.
02:42 Jordan: We'll attach SOC2 report, pen test summary, and an integration note for KMS. For full HSM/KMS integration (customer-managed keys) that's part of Redwood Private — we'll map the steps.
02:53 Priya: Also audit log format — we need event-level logs for data access and admin ops for at least 365 days. Is that configurable?
03:01 Samir: Yes — we expose structured audit logs; retention is an add-on. We can provide a sample schema. Note that when data is in Private, logs can be forwarded to your SIEM directly.
03:13 Liam: Samir, about the benchmark — we can share a set of representative prompts. The flows are heavy on embeddings+chat — two-step pipelines where embeddings happen upstream and the chat model uses a 3k token context often.
03:26 Samir: Good to know. For the 3k workflows we'll measure both cold-context latency and steady-state with KV cache warm. The biggest lever is model choice and quantization — moving from fp16 to int8 improves throughput but can change quality.
03:40 Maya: We care about quality. If int8 causes hallucination increases, that's a problem. Any guidance on where Redwood sits on quality vs cost?
03:48 Samir: We have recommended quantization profiles per model/workload; for many retrieval-augmented chat patterns int8 is fine. We'll label expected regen rates. Part of the pilot is to run your eval prompts to measure quality diffs.
04:02 Jordan: To manage risk, our SOW can include a pausable rollout and an evaluation gate: if quality drops beyond agreed thresholds we fall back to a higher-precision variant automatically.
04:12 Priya: Encryption-in-transit and at-rest — we need certificate rotation policy and KMS access logs. For customer-managed keys, who has the ability to rotate and who can request key deletion?
04:24 Jordan: In Private mode, keys are in your KMS, you control rotation and deletion — Redwood only has a wrapped key (envelope) and key access is not possible without your consent. We'll provide the exact mechanics in the KMS runbook.
04:36 Maya: Great. For the EU region staging — is there a checklist we can follow so we can prep infra on our side?
04:44 Nina: Yes — I'll share a staging checklist: network ranges, peering, firewall rules, test endpoints, sample payloads for perf tests, and roles for the SRE teams. Also a calendar with typical provisioning milestones.
04:55 Liam: One more question: failover. If eu-west is overloaded, can traffic route to a nearby region with acceptable latency, or do you insist on regional routing?
05:06 Samir: We have smart routing policies. You can configure priority: prefer regional, then nearby region fallback, then lower-cost hosted model. We recommend a threshold-based reroute at 800ms tail to preserve user experience. That policy can be tested in the pilot.
05:20 Maya: Competitor question — MegaAI told us they can do private EU deployment faster, but support SLA was weak. We want a partner who's responsive.
05:29 Jordan: We hear that a lot — we'll make sure the SOW includes support response times for P1–P3 and escalation path. We can also offer a short overlap of on-call coverage during the migration window.
05:40 Priya: Legal also asked about data retention and deletion for transcripts. If a user requests deletion, how quickly can you purge from caches and logs?
05:50 Samir: For hosted we have retention policies; purge requests propagate through the cache and storage within 24–72 hours depending on caching. In Private, you manage the retention. We'll document purge propagation behavior.
06:02 Jordan: Ok — to recap: commit to Dedicated for Q1 to hit your throughput and latency targets; run a Private/VPC pilot in parallel to validate KMS and compliance; we (Redwood) will provide SOC2, pen test, KMS runbook. Samir runs the perf tests with your prompts. Nina to send pricing scenarios.
06:18 Maya: That sounds right. Proposed dates? We need the revised pricing by next Friday, and the perf log within seven days after that.
06:26 Jordan: We'll aim to deliver pricing and SOW by 2026-12-10. Samir will start tests as soon as we get your prompt set; target send-back by 2026-12-14.
06:34 Nina: I'll also draft pilot success criteria and a detailed timeline for EU staging — will share by 2026-12-12.
06:40 Priya: I'll compile the compliance checklist and send any additional legal asks by 2026-12-09.
06:47 Jordan: Great. Any last questions?
06:50 Liam: Not right now, thanks.
06:52 Maya: No, appreciate this — please make the SOW explicit about migration costs.
06:56 Jordan: Will do — migration clause and rollback wording included. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
07:04 Meeting end.
